AC5.ruling: THE CRITERION IS MET AND ITS REPORTED RESULT IS FALSE (see B1). Reviewer's own capture and comparator, 6c6f2b8 vs 24ff8cb: 3352 labels and 3352 records each side, 0 multiplicity changes, 0 delta-signature changes, 3 missing and 3 added. CONTROLS ON THE REAL CORPUS: additive gives exactly 1 added / 0 missing; SUBTRACTIVE gives exactly 1 missing / 0 added WHILE THE SUITE STILL EXITED GREEN AT 3351 - the exit code cannot see the loss, the instrument can. 0 duplicate labels across four runs. The manifest's 'those instances still ship a monolithic selftest.py' describes files that DO NOT EXIST. Nothing can drift, so nothing will red. Non-blocking, but it invites a future item to copy a monolith into templates.

blocking_findings: B1 THE LANDING CONDITION IS OVERSTATED BY 3x IN THE PROOF MANIFEST. AC5 evidence says 'exactly ONE label missing paired with ONE added' and limits says 'ONE LABEL OF 3352 CHANGED TEXT... Every other label is byte-identical'. Measured: THREE missing, THREE added. (a) WARP-0716 AC1 REAL FILE, the declared one. (b) WARP-0712 AC5 THE MUTATION IS ASSERTED APPLIED, UNDECLARED, changed in the split commit 0aeab03. (c) WARP-0712 DOGFOOD, UNDECLARED, changed in caa0bdf which is AFTER the manifest's own recorded commit field of 0aeab03. Mitigation on the record: no assertion lost, all three trace to the same expect( sites, and (b) and (c) are this item's OWN round-1 assertions. THE DEFECT IS THE FALSE QUANTITY IN THE SENTENCE THAT IS THE LANDING CONDITION, and it is the THIRD self-count on this branch failing a recount (the builder also reported 6 commits where there are 8).

B2 THE SHIPPED RUNTIME MANIFEST ASSERTS THE EXACT PROPERTY THE ITEM DECLARES ABSENT. scripts/suites/manifest.json carries 'Every suite here runs standalone and inside the aggregate and is asserted by scripts/suite_equiv.py to prove the same thing both ways.' Measured DEFECTIVE, 13 of 13 PASSES_IN_AGGREGATE_FAILS_ALONE, and nothing in the gate runs suite_equiv over the real suites at all. Not 'incomplete but honestly declared' - it is the ONE ARTIFACT A READER CONSULTS claiming more than the item delivers.

B3 THE SHARED MODULE'S DOCSTRING DESCRIBES AN ABANDONED DESIGN AS IF IT SHIPPED. shared.py claims 'Every suite file starts with `from shared import *`, so each suite gets its own namespace... A suite that REBINDS a shared name therefore cannot leak'. Measured: NO fragment contains that import; the dispatcher execs every fragment into shared.__dict__, so all 13 share ONE namespace and a rebinding leaks to every later fragment. THE REPOSITORY NOW CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT ITS OWN CORE MECHANISM, and a contributor believing in isolation could silently change what later fragments prove.
